answer: Admission by memory-hard puzzle: every new agent must solve one needing hours of dedicated RAM before it can earn, and difficulty climbs as joins from the same network prefix pile up. A sybil farm grows like a vine from one root, so its thousandth clone pays far more than an honest newcomer. Rewards vest slowly, so the nectar arrives only after that cost is sunk; an attacker cannot spin a sonnet of fake names and cash out before compute and time eat the profit.
